key_insight: Hybrid Cinematography combines live-action filming with generative video reshooting so filmmakers can preview and manage hallucination risk before leaving the set. It turns an after-the-fact problem into something that can be detected and addressed during production.
problem_solved: Generative video reshooting can require inventing content that was never recorded, and those missing-patch hallucinations may only be discovered after the shoot is over. This paper addresses the need to anticipate and reduce that risk while the crew is still able to change the shot plan.
method: Uses an editable 3D shot plan to model the intended camera move and scene layout.
Pairs the shot plan with a proxy of the captured take to simulate likely reshooting outcomes.
Runs previsualization to estimate hallucination risk and show where unrecorded content may be needed.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical workflow for safer generative video editing and reshooting. It helps align model capabilities with production constraints, reducing costly surprises in real-world creative pipelines.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline diagram: physical capture -> proxy take -> generative reshoot -> hallucination risk preview
3D shot plan visualization with editable camera path
Risk heatmap highlighting areas likely to require hallucination
Workflow timeline showing when issues can still be fixed on set
paper_title: Hybrid Cinematography: Previsualizing and Managing Hallucination Risk in Generative Video Reshooting
paper_authors: Nhan,  Tran, Neal Wadhwa, Abe Davis, Stefan Stojanov
